title: Edge VPC install compatibility and triage notes
content:
Purpose and audience
- Quick reference for engineers running edge/VPC on-prem upgrades and initial installs where Terraform modules touch networking, GPU drivers, and runtime images.
- Focus: fast triage patterns, compatibility notes for TF modules, small smoke probes to run after bootstrap, and a minimal rollback checklist.

Context/constraints to keep in mind
- Many customers have transit/bastion setups and MTU differences (9000 vs 1500). GRPC + long sequences are sensitive to MTU fragmentation.
- On-prem images may be pulled from internal registries requiring imagePullSecrets; failing pulls are common when CIDR egress rules are tight.
- GPU stacks vary: driver version vs CUDA toolkit vs container runtime (nvidia-container-toolkit or nvidia-docker2) mismatch is the single largest cause of failed runtime allocations.
- Terraform state locking: customers often use S3-compatible storage with eventual consistency; plan/apply races are real during rolling upgrades.

Preflight checklist (quick run, 10–15m)
- Verify node conditions: kubectl get nodes -o wide (Ready, disk pressure, memory pressure)
- Check kubelet cgroup driver match: journalctl -u kubelet | grep cgroup (cgroupfs vs systemd mismatch => image pulls and runtime errors)
- Validate container runtime: crictl ps / crictl info => containerd/runtime version; confirm snapshotter (overlayfs vs zfs) supported by our daemon images
- GPU quick check: nvidia-smi && nvidia-container-cli --version (if present)
- Network check: ping between nodes, check MTU (ip link show), confirm iptables/nftables conntrack limits (cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max)
- Registry check: curl --head <registry>/v2/ and test image pull with crictl/pod that uses imagePullSecret
- Disk/IO: df -h and iostat -x 1 3 for hot partitions

Minimal smoke probes (run after install/bootstrap finishes)
- API health: curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health | jq .
- Simple model run: curl --data '{"prompt":"hello"}' http://localhost:8080/v1/generate -s --max-time 10
- GPU allocation: run a small container image with CUDA sample (docker run --gpus all --rm nvidia/cuda:11.8-base nvidia-smi)
- KV cache exercise: send two identical requests with different seed and measure response time; second should be noticeably faster if cache prefix worked

Terraform module compatibility notes (practical examples)
- module.network: prefer explicit mtu var (mtu = var.mtu) — do not assume 9000. Add a provider-level validation: validate that MTU is accepted by cloud on customer infra before applying heavy changes.
- module.nodes: when upgrading AMI/container image, use create_before_destroy = true for ASG-like constructs or rely on max_unavailable in kube rolling update strategy for minimal disruption.
- remote state: customers using S3-compatible backends need versioning enabled; add preflight that checks last-modified timestamp and locks via consul or dynamodb to avoid concurrent applies.
- provider versions: pin registry and provider versions in root; churn in provider minor versions has broken kube resources. Example: required_providers { kubernetes = { source = "hashicorp/kubernetes" version = "~> 2.17" } }

Common failure fingerprints and quick hypotheses
- Symptom: pods stuck ImagePullBackOff immediately after node bootstrap
  Hypothesis: registry egress blocked or imagePullSecret misconfigured
  Quick fix: check pod events kubectl describe pod; try crictl pull <image> from node, confirm DNS and SNI routing for registry.

- Symptom: container tries to start but fails with "failed to allocate memory" or OOMKilled on multi-model inference
  Hypothesis: host swap enabled or incorrect memory limits/cgroups, or device plugin failing to advertise GPU memory
  Quick fix: check dmesg for OOM, disable swap (swapoff -a) and ensure kubelet configured to respect systemReserved for memory.

- Symptom: gRPC calls hang intermittently under load; requests succeed eventually
  Hypothesis: MTU/fragmentation or iptables conntrack exhaustion
  Quick fix: verify MTU on path, raise net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max, tune conntrack timeout for established flows.

- Symptom: nvidia-smi reports no GPUs inside container even though host sees them
  Hypothesis: missing nvidia-container-toolkit or misconfigured runtimeClass/containerRuntime
  Quick fix: verify nvidia-container-runtime is present, daemon.json has correct runtimes, and kube device plugin daemonset is running and healthy.

- Symptom: terraform apply hangs during provider API call and then fails with partial changes
  Hypothesis: state lock or backend eventual consistency
  Quick fix: confirm remote state lock status, revert to manual lock/unlock, or run terraform apply with -target to isolate affected modules and avoid broad changes.

Upgrade/rollout play (short form)
- Canary roll: upgrade 1 node in a 10-node pool, run smoke probes for 10 minutes, verify latency P99 and error rate for endpoints tied to that node.
- Terraform approach: run terraform plan, inspect diff for node replace vs in-place change. If replace, consider using -target=module.nodes[0] for canary and then gradual plans.
- DB/stateful components: snapshot state, increase retention of logs for +48h, and enable debug tracing in the runtime to capture regressions.
- Fallback: have a recorded plan to revert images or Terraform revisions (git tag + terraform state backup). Document the exact target commands used for rollback.

Quick rollback commands (examples used in the field)
- terraform state pull > backup-state.json
- terraform apply -target=module.runtime[0] -var 'image_tag=stable-2024-09'
- kubectl rollout undo daemonset/runtime-daemonset --namespace redwood

Postmortem capture pointers (what to collect immediately)
- terraform plan output and apply logs (full stdout)
- kube events and pod logs for 5m window surrounding failure
- dmesg and journalctl -u kubelet and -u containerd around timestamps
- nvidia-smi -q and device-plugin logs
- network packet capture (tcpdump) for a failing request if gRPC hangs suspected

Small automation snippets to add to next TF module iteration (ideas)
- healthcheck module that deploys a small daemonset which runs the smoke probes above and reports pass/fail into a k8s CRD
- provider validation step that pings registry and checks MTU before resource changes
- terraform runbook generator: produce the subset of applies needed for canary via tags and -target flags automatically

Open items / followups
- Add a short section in module.network to detect and warn on MTU mismatch during plan.
- Create a small internal image with cuda sanity tests so customers without internet can run quick GPU checks.
- Add a CI job that runs an automated canary upgrade in a VLAN-isolated env to exercise the TF module changes.

Notes to self (raw, keep in doc for next edit)
- customers in EU with private registries often require explicit TLS SNI hostnames; add example for insecure registries in docs
- check interplay between kubelet eviction thresholds and our runtime memory limits — seen one site evict inference pods unexpectedly
- add a quick list of useful commands (crictl, ctr, kubectl exec ns/pod -- nvidia-smi) into a one-liner cheat sheet

End
